_mode_note: LIVE as of 2026-08-19 ~19:20 UTC, btc first (staged: eth, then sol, each after the previous is stable for ~a day). Shadow verified on all three coins: correct token per side vs gamma, exact dollar math, caps respected; btc's clean hour showed 243 signals with zero pricing-integrity rejections. risk._micro_note: Two live strategies on a ~$68 wallet. The risk block is GLOBAL, not per-strategy, so this sizes the COMBINED book: 3 concurrent x $12 = $36 worst-case committed, about half the bankroll, with the rest as settlement buffer. They rarely collide -- jumpscalp fires in a market's first 5s and is flat within 30s; rollavg fires in its last 30s. Daily stop $20: jumpscalp alone runs ~63 trades/day at 20sh, so a normal day swings roughly +/-$13 around an expected +$26 -- a tighter stop would fire on noise, a looser one is a third of the wallet.
risk._risk_note: Sized as a SYSTEM 2026-08-22: at size 15/$15 cap the honest print-capped sim runs ~$15-20/day with daily sd ~$20; the $50 stop is ~2.5 sigma, so it fires on a broken edge, not on the routine losing streaks that precede the cheap-band 5x winners (23% hit rate there is BY DESIGN -- break-even is the entry price). The old 20 stop was HALF a daily sd at the old size: it would have stopped the strategy on ordinary variance, collecting the 77% of cheap losers and being dark for the wins. max_market_shares 25 -> 200: the venue's price improvement fills more shares than sized (limit 0.53 -> fill 0.17 = 3x shares) and the DOLLAR cap is the real exposure bound; a low share cap only blocks the cheap band's deployment. Worst case per market stays = dollars committed = $15. Needs ~$60 balance for 3 concurrent; scale caps and stop TOGETHER, linearly, when the bankroll grows.
risk._rung_note: RUNG 0, sized to the ~$60 balance 2026-08-22: locked 25 sh (~$25/market, two markets can be in flight between buy and redeem, so ~$54 peak against ~$60 cash -- occasional balance rejections just skip a trade). Tape sim: ~$60/day, worst day -$14, 2/9 days negative. Deposit ladder: $250 -> locked 50 / cap 55 / stop 80; $700 -> 150/160/200; $1.8k -> 400/420/500. Advance a rung only after >=100 locked fills realise within 0.5c of tape (src/pnl.py); scale cap and stop with size.

rollavg_edge._disabled_note: OFF as of 2026-08-20: the endgame taker is retired from live. Micro-live measured its structural problem directly -- adverse fill selection (171 kills vs 14 fills; fills avg px 0.296 vs paper 0.857) -- and the filtered variant traded too rarely to pay for its tail risks. EarlyBird replaces it as the sole real-money strategy: same model, opposite end of the window, where the book is two-sided and the strike is already formed. Retiring it also frees both concurrency slots for consecutive EarlyBird holds and removes the endgame-only failure paths (concurrent unknown resolutions on one token, post-drop orphan fills). The paper bot keeps the unfiltered endgame as the frozen control for live_vs_paper.
rollavg_edge._size_note: 10 shares (~$9 at typical fill px) against paper's 100. Every GATE is identical to the frozen paper config -- same zmin, same max_price, same window -- so live and paper disagree only about execution, which is the one thing micro-live exists to measure. The venue min is 5 shares; risk room below that is logged as live_miss/below_venue_min, not sent.
rollavg_edge._require_edge_note: ON for LIVE as of 2026-08-20 (paper keeps it OFF as the control). Live measured adverse fill selection the tape cannot show: 171 kills vs 14 fills overnight, with fills averaging px 0.296 vs paper's 0.857 -- the venue fills us eagerly when the quote is going bad and starves us when it's right. require_edge only buys when ask <= empirical_fair - edge_min (2c), the pre-measured +10.15c/sh filter (3x per-share edge on ~1/5 volume): trades that are mispriced in OUR favor, which adverse selection cannot punish. The divergence report A/Bs this against the unfiltered paper baseline.
rollavg_edge._relaunch_note: RE-ENABLED 2026-08-21 with the padded marketable limit. It was retired on 08-20 for adverse fill selection; that turned out to be an EXECUTION defect (unpadded limit + a round() that put the limit UNDER the ask above 0.96), not a defect of the prediction. Print-proof pooled: +5.51c/sh t=3.02, 7/9 days positive, holdout Aug18-21 +4.44c/sh; ~25 trades/day at the current micro caps. Entries skew cheap (avg 0.213) so per-trade variance is high: the daily stop, not the per-trade size, is the real risk control.
rollavg_edge._gate_note: PAPER gate, unchanged: require_edge false, max_price 0.99, zmin 2.0. This is the configuration to fix and measure, not to redesign. It was briefly switched to require_edge after four live trades lost -- a 4-fill sample against a 628-fill measurement (+3.24c/sh, t=2.99, 8/9 days positive) on a strategy whose per-share sd is 34c. That override was not justified by the evidence and is reverted. Capacity note: the deep book sits at 0.96-0.99 (10k+ shares resting, book probe median depth 33,767), which is exactly the band this gate trades, so size is limited by the edge holding at scale, not by liquidity.
rollavg_edge._zmin_note: 2.0 -> 1.5 on 2026-08-22 after the 8-day holdout verification (src/endgame_lab.py, 2259 markets, print-proof fills, 40% time holdout): z1.5 HOLDOUT +3.07c/sh (t=2.3, n=246) vs z2.0 +2.25c (t=1.4, n=163) -- ~50% more trades at equal-or-better per-share edge, and 1/9 negative days vs 2/9 in the dollar sim. zmin 2.5/3.0 look better in-sample and FAIL the holdout (-0.12c, -0.93c): the tighter gates were overfit. require_edge also fails holdout (+1.67c t=0.4 vs +9.39c in-sample) and stays off.
rollavg_edge._ladder_note: SIZE LADDER for the locked band (>=0.90), 2026-08-22. Capacity there is resting depth (book probe median 33,767 executable shares; 10k+ per tick observed), not prints, so it scales -- but edge at size is unproven live, so climb in rungs: 50 -> 150 -> 400, advancing only after >=100 locked fills realise within 0.5c of the tape's +1.8c/share (check with src/pnl.py). Each rung also scales max_market_dollars and daily_loss_limit proportionally. If realised collapses at a rung, the ladder found the real capacity: step back.

_latency_note: Used by the paper half of shadow mode only. In live mode no simulated latency is added: the venue's real 250ms hold and the real Amsterdam rtt replace the model.

zmaker._note: MEASUREMENT ONLY -- simulated against real trade prints in an isolated ledger (maker_fills.jsonl / maker_sim_settled lines), never touching the real-money broker or risk. Rationale: 24h of live takers measured adverse fill selection (171 kills vs 14 fills; fills at avg 0.296 vs paper 0.857) -- the favourite's ask side empties in the final 30s, so the taker leg starves where the edge is largest. The maker leg rests a bid at fair-minus-3c on the favoured side, TTL 10s, cancel-and-replace, never resting into the final 3s. Maker fills on prints are the HONEST direction of simulation (prints are executed volume). If a few days measure it positive at meaningful volume, the real maker executor gets built.

Pre-committed holdout (Aug 15-20, paginated tape, 1594 btc / 1467 sol markets): btc zmin0.5 +3.98c/sh t=0.82 (bar was +5c), as-deployed-with-strike-latch +1.96c, at the live sigma threshold +0.23c ~= zero; sol +2.97c t=0.88, 3/6 days. _taker_pad_note: Marketable-limit padding: the fix for one-way fill selection. A CLOB fills a taker at the RESTING maker's price and this venue re-validates after its 250ms taker hold, so a limit set to exactly the ask we saw dies to any uptick in flight -- meaning we filled when the price fell (wrong) and were killed when it rose (right). Measured live: 171 kills / 14 fills, fills avg 0.296 vs paper 0.857. Padding pays the ask when the book is unchanged and still matches when it moved, Bounded three ways: relative to price (taker_pad_rel, so a flat 5c cannot become a 167% overpay on a 3c ask), absolutely (taker_pad), and by value (paying the limit in full must still leave taker_pad_min_edge after fee). Sizing runs on the PADDED limit because a BUY here is rate-based -- size x limit is the cash committed -- so the per-market dollar cap binds on money that can actually leave. Print-proof measurement, 6788 markets x 3 coins x 9 days: fill rate 68->89% (btc), 44->67% (eth), 33->54% (sol); pooled deployed gate +3.37c/sh t=1.75 -> +5.51c/sh t=3.02.
_probe_note: Probe config: identical gate and padding to config.live.json, sized so an hour of real orders answers the fill question for a few dollars. Graduate to config.live.json sizing only after the measured kill:fill ratio beats 5:1.
_desync_note: Blocks a signal whose price disagrees with the venue's OWN last print by more than this. Replaces a model-disagreement check that silently halved the strategy: calib.py's p_up spans [0.1833, 0.9159], so a Down contract can never be valued above 0.8167 and every Down favourite at 0.97-0.99 scored ev -0.17 and was blocked, while the identical Up trade at -0.075 passed. Measured live: 10 blocks, all Down. The guard's real job is a frozen book view (launch day: ours stuck at 0.99 while the venue traded 0.022), which a print comparison catches directly.

jumpscalp._note: PRE-OPEN entry at t-20..t-10, exit +9c or flat 30s later, never at settlement. Direction from the sign of z with 10s momentum required to agree. HONEST out-of-sample btc, signals computed strictly as of the decision moment: +2.78c/sh t=4.9 at t-20, +2.64c t=5.4 at t-10, +2.65c t=5.6 at t0. An earlier measurement claimed +5.45c t=24.7 for the pre-open entry; it read spot and momentum AT t0 to decide at t-20, i.e. 20 seconds of look-ahead, and the 'earlier is much better' decay it produced was the leak's fingerprint. Corrected, pre-open and at-open are about equal and the edge is roughly half. Pre-open is kept because the book there is verifiably deep (643sh at the touch, 250sh at 0.00c slippage). NOT ESTABLISHED on eth/sol; btc only.
jumpscalp._entry_note: AT the open, t+0..t+3. The pre-open window was chosen on a look-ahead artifact; scored at the decision instant it is +0.00 to +0.66 c/sh (t~1) while t+0..t+3 is +1.21 to +2.19 (t 2.2-4.3) and t+4 falls to +0.24. See src/jumpscalp_preopen.py.
jumpscalp._off_note: OFF 2026-08-22 at the account owner's instruction after 4 live trades (+2.72 on three winners, -5.11 on one deadline exit, net -2.39). The entry and exit chain is working end to end; this is a decision about variance, not a defect. Re-enable by flipping the flag -- strategy code, tests and measurements are all left in place.

_incident_note: 2026-08-22 20:14 UTC drawdown, -$45.89 on the day. Two causes, both mine: (1) families carried 15m, which NO verification covered -- the 8-day holdout study was --fam 5m only, so 15m markets were trading an unvalidated gate; (2) the 4:00-4:15 15m market and the 4:10-4:15 5m market OVERLAP IN TIME and both bought Up, so one wrong directional call cost -13.03 and -18.41 together while max_concurrent_markets counted them as two independent markets. Restricting to 5m fixes both: consecutive 5m endgame windows never overlap. Sizes cut to fit the REMAINING balance (~$23 after the drawdown, not the ~$60 rung 0 was built for) and the daily stop dropped to 15 to match. Re-raise only after the balance supports it AND src/pnl.py shows the 5m-only config tracking tape.
